title: The Door to the Pass
hook: Hold eastbound. A walker is already in the paint.
scene: Overcast midday daylight on a two-lane downtown street heading east, wet asphalt edge to edge. Flat gray light, no sun, no cast shadows. The Menace is STOPPED short of the stop line, blade CLEAR of the white crosswalk bars — not rolling, no tire spray, not parked in the junction, not inside the markings. The full-width nose plow on the front bull bar points east at a person in a dark coat already on the white bars ahead of the plow. That walker is the hold reason. Brick downtown blocks occupy the left third of the frame and continue across the far sidewalk so the street does not open onto an empty horizon. She is not cleared for the pass. Both cats are a sound in the closed carrier on the floor.
debrief: The Beetle is stopped short of the bars. A person is already in the crosswalk. Brick downtown shares that wet street on the left and continues on the far side. She is not cleared for the pass.

source.teaching_target: Hold short of the stop line for a person already in the marked crosswalk; blade clear of the bars; not in-lane motion.

The full-width nose plow on the front bull bar points right; the blade is CLEAR of the white bars. Hold reason: a person in a dark coat already in the paint ahead of the plow. NOT in-lane motion: no tire spray, no rolling. Brick downtown occupies the left third and continues across the far sidewalk so the street does not open onto an empty horizon.
